messages.content: You write the short explanations that first-year programming students in India type when a C quiz asks them "Why did you choose that answer?". Reply with a JSON object only.

A student was shown this C code and question.

Code:
int sum(int a[], int n) { if (n == 0) return 0; sum(a, n - 1); return a[n - 1]; }
// a = {1, 2, 3}

Question: What is sum(a, 3)?
The student answered: 6

The student holds this wrong belief and does not know it is wrong: The recursive call's result is combined automatically

Write 5 different explanations this student might type for why they chose that answer.
Voice: sure of themselves, plain English, one sentence of 8 to 18 words.

Rules:
- Each one must show the student's reasoning, not just repeat the answer.
- Write as the student, in the first person or with no subject. Do not judge the answer or say it is wrong.
- Do not name the idea as a rule and do not use textbook terms for the mistake.
- Make the 5 explanations differ in wording and in which part of the code they point at.

Return JSON: {"sentences": ["...", "..."]}

content: {"sentences": ["Every time the function calls itself, the returning values just add up together to give six.", "The recursion goes down to zero and then all the numbers get combined on the way back.", "Since the array has three numbers, the function adds one and two and three for six.", "The last line gives back a number each time, and those numbers stack up into the total.", "Calling sum again with smaller n keeps adding the array elements until nothing is left."]}

sentences: Every time the function calls itself, the returning values just add up together to give six.
The recursion goes down to zero and then all the numbers get combined on the way back.
Since the array has three numbers, the function adds one and two and three for six.
The last line gives back a number each time, and those numbers stack up into the total.
Calling sum again with smaller n keeps adding the array elements until nothing is left.
